summary: IDS feed s146_double is degraded: 82% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% tolerance and 7.4% jumbo frames exceed 1518-byte IDS MTU and are dropped, both severely reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: 82% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) vs IDS tolerance of 60%; traffic is forwarded without broker-based decryption or key sharing, so payload is opaque to IDS signatures.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to majority of payloads; signature matching, anomaly detection and full-payload inspection fail for ~82% of traffic, creating large detection gaps.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS at packet broker / SSL visibility appliance and forward cleartext to IDS, or selectively filter encrypted traffic that IDS cannot inspect, to restore payload visibility within tool tolerance.

findings.root_cause: 242 of 3254 frames (7.4%) exceed IDS port MTU of 1518 bytes (largest 8058 bytes) - jumbo frames delivered without fragmentation; IDS 1G NIC silently drops oversized frames.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS misses 7.4% of frames entirely, breaking flow reassembly and allowing large-payload attacks to evade detection; IDS needs full payload so drops are worse than truncation.

recommended_fix.why: Enable jumbo-frame support (MTU 9000) on IDS capture port and broker egress, or configure broker to fragment/slice to 1518 bytes, to prevent silent NIC drops while preserving as much payload as possible for IDS that requires full payload.
